t:
(a) In General.—This Act and the amendments made by this Act shall not affect or diminish the rights and obligations of the Secretary of the Interior and private parties under agreements in existence on the date of enactment of this Act, except to the extent that the agreements are renewed or extended after that date. 
    (b) Delivery.—No agreement described in subsection (a) shall affect or diminish the right of any party that purchases helium after the date of enactment of this Act in accordance with section 6 of the Helium Act (50 U.S.C. 167d) (as amended by section 5) to receive delivery of the helium in accordance with section 5(e)(2) of the Helium Act (50 U.S.C. 167c(e)(2)) (as amended by section 4).

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the mention of "private parties" and "agreements" with the Secretary signals outside involvement in a federal decision. But this is only a savings clause that preserves existing contractual rights and helium delivery rights. It creates no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue over a federal decision.
fable.s: shall not affect or diminish the rights and obligations of the Secretary of the Interior and private parties under agreements in existence on the date of enactment of this Act

opus.w: This is a savings clause. It keeps existing helium agreements between the Secretary and private parties in force and protects buyers' delivery rights. Mentioning private parties and agreements is tempting, but nothing here has outsiders consult, comment, or advise before a federal decision, and it creates no right to sue over one. It only preserves existing contract rights.
opus.s: This Act and the amendments made by this Act shall not affect or diminish the rights and obligations of the Secretary of the Interior and private parties under agreements in existence on the date of enactment of this Act

qwen_chat.w: The section preserves existing agreements but does not require any new consultation, coordination, or participation by private parties in federal decision-making. It merely states that existing contracts remain valid and are not diminished by the new Act. There is no procedural requirement for the government to engage with outsiders before making a decision.
qwen_chat.s: This Act and the amendments made by this Act shall not affect or diminish the rights and obligations of the Secretary of the Interior and private parties under agreements in existence on the date of enactment of this Act
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "private parties" are involved in agreements, and thus there is participation. However, the text explicitly states that the Act does *not* affect existing agreements, and it does not require any new consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving these private parties. It merely preserves the status quo of existing contracts. There is no requirement for the government to consult with outsiders before making a decision; it simply acknowledges that existing contracts remain valid.
